title: The Plantation Days show and James P. Johnson's band
summary: Leonard Harper produced the show and James P. Johnson led a ten-to-twelve piece band that played in the pit and on stage.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What kind of a show was this show that you went to Europe with?
I think it's good. What kind of a show was this show that you went to Europe with? What was it called again?

Plantation Days. Yeah. You know who launched Deez in New York? No. Barbara Deez? No. Well, he produced it. And, no, I beg your pardon, Leonard Harper. You remember Leonard Harper, don't you? No. That's right, I forget. That's New York. I bet your brother knew. He produced the shows. James P. Johnson had the band.
He was the leader of the band?

Well, it was Charles Elgar's band. Elgar couldn't leave, you know, because he had too much. He had studio and different things there in Chicago. And James P. took hold of the band. He came. The whole band?

22 pieces? No, no, no, no. That band was cut out. Because you see we went to Tom Schmauer's Green Mill Gardens with the show. That's where we opened up at. Then when it came time to go on the road we brought the show in in the theater to get used to the stage and everything. And James P., a lot of his music we were using. Going through your- You were the pit band? Well, we were the pit band and we got up on the stage after intermission. Wow, what, ten, twelve pieces?
How many were you? What do you have? Wow. Wow.
It could be twelve. Easy. And James P. was the leader of the band? Yeah, might be- might have been more than that but I don't remember.
